8	/-!
9	# The projective line over a field, with usable charts
10	
11	We define `AlgebraicGeometry.P1 k` as `Proj` of the standard graded polynomial ring
12	`k[X₀, X₁]` (`MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k` with the degree grading), together with:
13	
14	* `P1.structureMap : P1 k ⟶ Spec (.of k)`, and the instance `IsProper (P1.structureMap k)`
15	  (inherited from mathlib's properness of `Proj`);
16	* the two standard affine charts `D₊(X₀)`, `D₊(X₁)` (`P1.chartOpen`), which cover `P1 k`
17	  (`P1.chartOpen_sup`), together with the open immersions `P1.chartι i` from the affine
18	  models `Spec (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀`;
19	* identifications of the chart section rings with polynomial rings:
20	  `P1.awayAlgEquiv : (k[X₀,X₁]_(Xᵢ))₀ ≃ₐ[k] k[t]` (the coordinate is `t = Xⱼ/Xᵢ`).
21	
22	The identification of the chart *overlap* with Laurent polynomials, the section-level
23	versions, and the bundled chart package `AlgebraicGeometry.LaurentChartPair` are in the
24	continuation file `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1Charts`.
25	
26	The generic instance `Algebra R (HomogeneousLocalization 𝒜 x)` (for a graded `R`-algebra) and
27	the lemma `LaurentPolynomial.exists_toLaurent_add_aeval` (*Laurent span*: every Laurent
28	polynomial is the sum of a polynomial in `T` and a polynomial in `T⁻¹`) are general-purpose
29	and live in their natural namespaces.
30	
31	## Implementation notes
32	
33	We install `MvPolynomial.gradedAlgebra` as a (project-global) instance: everywhere in this
34	project, `MvPolynomial` carries the standard degree grading. Mathlib leaves this to the user
35	because other gradings exist; this project only ever uses the standard one.
36	-/

60	/-- **Laurent span**: every Laurent polynomial is the sum of a polynomial in `T` and a
61	polynomial in `T⁻¹`. -/
62	theorem exists_toLaurent_add_aeval {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R] (f : R[T;T⁻¹]) :
63	    ∃ p q : Polynomial R, f = p.toLaurent + Polynomial.aeval (T (-1) : R[T;T⁻¹]) q := by
64	  induction f using LaurentPolynomial.induction_on' with
65	  | add p q hp hq =>
66	    obtain ⟨p₁, q₁, rfl⟩ := hp
67	    obtain ⟨p₂, q₂, rfl⟩ := hq
68	    exact ⟨p₁ + p₂, q₁ + q₂, by simp only [map_add]; ring⟩
69	  | C_mul_T n a =>
70	    rcases le_or_gt 0 n with hn | hn
71	    · refine ⟨Polynomial.C a * Polynomial.X ^ n.toNat, 0, ?_⟩
72	      rw [map_zero, add_zero, Polynomial.toLaurent_C_mul_X_pow, Int.toNat_of_nonneg hn]
73	    · refine ⟨0, Polynomial.C a * Polynomial.X ^ (-n).toNat, ?_⟩
74	      rw [map_zero, zero_add, map_mul, Polynomial.aeval_C, map_pow, Polynomial.aeval_X,

76	      congr 2

11	
12	Two groups of results about `P1 k` feeding the construction of the finite map `C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
13	
14	**Morphisms into `ℙ¹` from an element of a ring.**  For a ring `A` under `k` (a morphism
15	`ρ : k ⟶ A` of rings) and an element `a : A`, `P1.fromSpecChart k ρ i a : Spec A ⟶ P1 k` is
16	the morphism through the chart `D₊(Xᵢ)` sending the chart coordinate to `a`:
17	
18	* `P1.fromSpecChart_structureMap`: it is a morphism over `k`;
19	* `P1.SpecMap_fromSpecChart`: it is natural in `A`;
20	* `P1.fromSpecChart_isUnit`: **the gluing identity** — for a unit `u`, the morphism
21	  `[1 : u]` through chart `0` equals the morphism `[u⁻¹ : 1]` through chart `1`.  This is
22	  the entire content of "the loci `U_f` and `U_{1/f}` glue to a morphism to `ℙ¹`",
23	  concentrated in a single point-free identity: both morphisms factor through the chart
24	  overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)`, where they are induced by the same ring homomorphism (the
25	  localization lift sending the overlap coordinate `T = X₁/X₀` to `u`).
26	* `P1.fromSpecChart_base_genericPoint`: if the evaluation `k[t] → A`, `t ↦ a` is injective
27	  ("`a` is transcendental"), the generic point of `Spec A` lands on the generic point of
28	  `ℙ¹`.

31	Dedekind section rings, so its specialization order has height one
32	(`P1.specializes_eq_genericPoint_or_eq`); and it has a point besides the generic one
33	(`P1.exists_ne_genericPoint`).  Consequently every non-generic point of `ℙ¹` is closed
34	(`P1.isClosed_singleton_of_ne_genericPoint`).

31	`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_one_le_classDeg_of_isFinite_toP1`: for a

33	degree-one cohomology of `𝒪(D)` vanishes for **every** divisor `D` of class `l · θⁿ`, for all
34	large `n`. The reduction of the worksheet §2.5, in the simplified `m = m₀` form:
35	
36	* run FLV-fiber (`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) on a divisor `D₀`
37	  realizing `l`: `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D₀ + m₀·F))`, `F` the fiber divisor, `d' := deg F ≥ 1`;
38	* for `n` large, the residual class `θⁿ · (𝒪(F))⁻ᵐ⁰` has degree `≥ 1 − χ(𝒪)`, so the Riemann
39	  inequality (`riemann_inequality`) gives a nonzero global section, hence an **effective**
40	  witness `E` of that class (`exists_effective_of_picClass`);
41	* `D₀ + m₀·F + E` is in class `l · θⁿ`; peeling `E` point-by-point transports `Subsingleton`

43	* witness-independence (W6-lite `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`) upgrades the single

8	/-!
9	# Spreading a transcendental rational function out to a morphism to `ℙ¹`
10	
11	On an integral scheme `X`, proper and smooth of relative dimension `1` over a field `k`
12	(a smooth projective curve), a rational function `f₀ ∈ K(X)` transcendental over `k`
13	spreads out to a `k`-morphism `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹` with finite fibers:
14	
15	* every stalk of `X` is a valuation ring of `K(X)`
16	  (`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.valuationRing_stalk`), so at every point `x` either `f₀` or
17	  `f₀⁻¹` is a regular germ; the corresponding chart morphism
18	  `Spec 𝒪_x ⟶ ℙ¹` (`P1.fromSpecChart`) agrees generically with the "generic point"
19	  morphism `Spec K(X) ⟶ ℙ¹` by the gluing identity `P1.fromSpecChart_units`;
20	* by the spreading-out theory of rational maps (`Scheme.RationalMap`), the generic
21	  morphism defines a rational map `X ⤏ ℙ¹` over `k` whose domain of definition therefore
22	  contains every point, and `Scheme.RationalMap.toPartialMap` glues it to a morphism
23	  `π : X ⟶ ℙ¹`;
24	* transcendence of `f₀` makes `π` send the generic point to the generic point, whence
25	  every fiber of `π` is finite: the fiber of the generic point is a set of closed points
26	  mapping onto the non-closed generic point of `ℙ¹` (impossible for the proper `π` unless
27	  the fiber is `{ξ}`), and any other fiber is a closed subset of the Noetherian
28	  curve avoiding the generic point, hence finite
29	  (`Scheme.finite_of_isClosed_of_notMem_genericPoint`).
30	
31	The main result is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_locallyQuasiFinite_isDominant_toP1` (with the
32	locally-quasi-finite-only projection `exists_locallyQuasiFinite_toP1` kept for the existing
33	finiteness consumer); it also records that `π` is **dominant**, read off from the
34	generic-point image. Zariski's main theorem (in `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.MapToP1`) upgrades
35	local quasi-finiteness to finiteness.
36	-/
